body.rationale: IPS status: ratified, as given in the prompt. Breaches therefore count as real. I am HRP and fail the volatility and tracking-error limits myself, so I weight hard compliance heavily. Only four candidates have no hard breaches: black_litterman, cvar_minimization, inverse_volatility and resampled_efficient_frontier. All four are in my top five. Risk_parity is the fifth, with only a narrow volatility shortfall (7.56% vs the 8% floor). 1) inverse_volatility: no breaches, effective N 14.8, backtest drawdown -22.9%, and no return forecast or tuned parameter, which fits the covariance-over-forecast preference seen in late-cycle regimes. The intra-category review found its arithmetic correct. The caveat is about 43% in correlated credit and sovereign sleeves, and the reviewers' point about equalised standalone risk is minor. 2) risk_parity: the closest risk-structured peer and a near-compliant covariance-aware portfolio. Reviews flag only framing errors (entropy of capital weights is not risk dispersion), and its volatility shortfall is small and fixable by blending. 3) resampled_efficient_frontier: compliant, diversified (N 13.1) and robust to forecast noise by construction. The drawdown is only 16bp inside the limit, which is fragile, so it ranks below the first two. 4) cvar_minimization: compliant, best drawdown of the compliant set (-18.7%) and a good backtest Sharpe (0.74). Its reviewers say volatility was tuned to exactly 8.00% and it has only 2.9 effective assets, so it is concentrated and should not be the CIO's anchor. It does add the non-traditional family. 5) black_litterman: compliant with N 5.7. Its reviewer found the equilibrium prior distorted by double-counted overlapping ETF AUM, and it rests on a stable stock-bond hedge (about 49% Treasuries, 44% equities). It sits fifth. First beats fifth because inverse_volatility achieves compliance with a lower drawdown (-22.9% vs -21.9% is close, but with 14.8 vs 5.7 effective assets) and without a flawed prior or forecast dependence. Black-Litterman's compliance depends on a questionable equilibrium vector and a stock-bond correlation assumption. The top five span four families (heuristic, risk_structured, return_optimized, non_traditional). Bottom flag: market_cap_weight. It has a -40.6% backtest drawdown against the -25% limit, the highest CRO risk score (0.80) and about 77% in equity. Reviewers showed its 'market portfolio' is ETF AUM with overlapping style sleeves, and the proposal itself calls it a diagnostic. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier. Its three breaches make it unsuitable as an anchor, but it is useful as an orthogonal ensemble member and is not the portfolio I least want the CIO to lean on.
